rules.title: SQL query built directly from user input
rules.description: A database query contains request data (GET, POST, REQUEST or COOKIE) without parameter binding.
rules.impact: An attacker can read, change or delete database data, bypass login, and in some setups run commands on the server.
rules.remediation: Use prepared statements with bound parameters (PDO::prepare + execute, or mysqli_prepare). Never concatenate request data into SQL.

rules.title: SQL query built with string concatenation or variable interpolation
rules.description: An SQL statement is assembled from variables. If any variable can contain user data, the query is injectable.
rules.impact: Possible SQL injection leading to data theft or modification.
rules.remediation: Replace string building with prepared statements and bound parameters. Whitelist table or column names that cannot be bound.

rules.title: Prepared statement text is built from variables
rules.description: prepare() is used, but the SQL text itself contains variables, which defeats the protection.
rules.impact: Possible SQL injection even though prepare() is present.
rules.remediation: Keep the SQL text constant and pass every value through placeholders (? or :name).

rules.title: Removed mysql_* functions are used
rules.description: The mysql_* extension was removed in PHP 7. Code using it only runs on very old, unsupported PHP versions and usually has no query parameterisation.
rules.impact: Runs on unsupported PHP with known vulnerabilities; encourages injectable queries.
rules.remediation: Migrate to PDO or mysqli with prepared statements and upgrade PHP to a supported version.

rules.title: User input printed to the page without escaping (XSS)
rules.description: Request data is written into the HTML response without htmlspecialchars().
rules.impact: Attackers can run JavaScript in a visitor's browser: steal sessions, deface pages, or perform actions as the victim.
rules.remediation: Escape all output: htmlspecialchars($value, ENT_QUOTES, "UTF-8"), or use a template engine with auto-escaping.

rules.title: $_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] used without escaping
rules.description: PHP_SELF contains attacker-controlled text from the URL and is commonly placed in form actions.
rules.impact: Reflected cross-site scripting.
rules.remediation: Use an empty action attribute or htmlspecialchars($_SERVER["PHP_SELF"], ENT_QUOTES).

rules.title: Shell command built from user input
rules.description: Request data is passed to a function that runs operating-system commands.
rules.impact: Attackers can run any command on the server (full server takeover).
rules.remediation: Avoid shell commands. If unavoidable, use fixed commands with escapeshellarg() on each argument and a strict whitelist.

rules.title: Shell command function called with a variable
rules.description: A command-execution function receives a variable. If the value is influenced by a user, commands can be injected.
rules.impact: Possible remote command execution.
rules.remediation: Validate against a whitelist and wrap each argument in escapeshellarg(), or replace the command with a PHP library.

rules.title: Backtick shell execution with a variable
rules.description: The backtick operator runs a shell command and here it contains a variable.
rules.impact: Possible remote command execution.
rules.remediation: Remove the backtick call or escape each argument with escapeshellarg().

rules.title: Code evaluated from user input
rules.description: Request data is executed as PHP code.
rules.impact: Complete remote code execution: the attacker controls the server.
rules.remediation: Never evaluate user input. Remove eval/assert/create_function and use real data structures or a whitelist of actions.

rules.title: eval() or similar dynamic code execution
rules.description: The code builds and runs PHP at runtime. This is risky and is also a typical sign of a backdoor.
rules.impact: Possible remote code execution.
rules.remediation: Replace with normal code, callbacks or a whitelist. Remove it if you do not recognise it.

rules.title: preg_replace with the /e modifier
rules.description: The /e modifier makes preg_replace execute the replacement as PHP code. It was removed in PHP 7.
rules.impact: Remote code execution when the subject or replacement contains user input.
rules.remediation: Use preg_replace_callback() with a real function instead.

rules.title: Function called dynamically from user input
rules.description: A function name or callable is chosen or fed from request data.
rules.impact: Attackers can call arbitrary PHP functions.
rules.remediation: Map allowed actions to fixed callbacks with a whitelist; never call a function name taken from a request.

rules.title: unserialize() on user input
rules.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
rules.description: Request data is passed to unserialize(), which can instantiate attacker-chosen objects.
rules.impact: Object injection that can lead to remote code execution or file deletion.
rules.remediation: Use json_decode() for data exchange. If unserialize is required, pass allowed_classes => false.

rules.title: unserialize() without allowed_classes
rules.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
rules.description: unserialize() is used on a variable. If the data can be influenced by a user, object injection is possible.
rules.impact: Possible object injection.
rules.remediation: Prefer json_decode(). Otherwise use unserialize($data, ["allowed_classes" => false]).

rules.title: Obfuscated eval (typical web shell / backdoor)
rules.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
rules.description: eval() runs decoded or decompressed text. Legitimate code almost never does this; malware and backdoors always do.
rules.impact: The file very likely contains a backdoor that gives an attacker full control of the server.
rules.remediation: Treat the server as compromised: remove the file, find how it got there, rotate all passwords and keys, and restore code from a trusted source.

rules.title: Request value used as a function name (web shell pattern)
rules.description: Code like $_POST["x"]($_POST["y"]) lets a remote visitor run any PHP function with any argument.
rules.impact: Remote code execution; this is the classic one-line web shell.
rules.remediation: Remove this code. Check the whole project and server for other injected files.

rules.title: Known web shell signature found
rules.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
rules.description: The text matches the name or marker of a publicly known web shell or hacking tool.
rules.impact: The project may contain or be derived from a backdoor, or the file may be a deliberate hacking tool.
rules.remediation: Review the file manually. If it is not intentional, remove it and investigate how it was added.

rules.title: Heavily obfuscated code
rules.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
rules.description: Very long encoded strings or character-by-character code building are used to hide what the code does.
rules.impact: Hidden malicious logic is possible.
rules.remediation: Decode and review the content. Replace with readable code or remove.

rules.title: File include controlled by user input (LFI/RFI)
rules.description: The path passed to include/require comes from the request.
rules.impact: Attackers can read local files or, with allow_url_include, run their own PHP code.
rules.remediation: Never include a path from user input. Map short keys to fixed files with a whitelist.

rules.title: include/require uses a variable path
rules.description: A file is included from a variable. If the variable can be influenced by a user, arbitrary files can be loaded.
rules.impact: Possible local or remote file inclusion.
rules.remediation: Use fixed paths or a whitelist of allowed files.

rules.title: Server makes a request to a user-supplied URL (SSRF)
rules.description: The server fetches a URL that comes from the request.
rules.impact: Attackers can make the server reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints or other hosts.
rules.remediation: Allow only whitelisted hosts, resolve and block private IP ranges, and disable redirects.

rules.title: File path or URL controlled by user input (path traversal / arbitrary file access)
rules.description: A file function receives a path taken from the request.
rules.impact: Attackers can read, overwrite or delete files outside the intended folder using ../ sequences.
rules.remediation: Use basename(), realpath() and verify the result starts with an allowed base directory, or use a whitelist of file ids.

rules.title: Uploaded file saved under the client-supplied name
rules.description: The original file name sent by the browser is used as the saved file name.
rules.impact: An attacker can upload a .php file and run it on the server.
rules.remediation: Generate a random file name, allow only specific extensions and MIME types, store uploads outside the web root.

rules.title: File upload without type checks
rules.description: move_uploaded_file is used and no extension or content-type check was found in this file.
rules.impact: Possible upload of executable scripts.
rules.remediation: Check the extension against a whitelist, verify content (finfo / getimagesize), use random names, and store outside the web root.

rules.title: Weak or fast hash used for passwords
rules.description: MD5, SHA-1 and plain SHA-2 are fast hashes that can be cracked quickly.
rules.impact: If the database leaks, most passwords can be recovered.
rules.remediation: Use password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT) and password_verify(). Rehash existing users at next login.

rules.title: Predictable random value used for a security token
rules.description: rand(), mt_rand(), uniqid() and time() are predictable and must not create secrets.
rules.impact: Attackers may guess reset links, tokens or keys.
rules.remediation: Use bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) or random_int().

rules.title: Obsolete or weak encryption algorithm
rules.description: mcrypt is removed from PHP, and DES, RC4 and ECB mode are broken or leak data patterns.
rules.impact: Encrypted data may be recovered or modified.
rules.remediation: Use openssl with aes-256-gcm (or libsodium) and a random IV/nonce.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.description: The code turns off certificate checking for HTTPS connections.
rules.impact: Man-in-the-middle attackers can read and change traffic.
rules.remediation: Remove the override and keep verification enabled; install the proper CA bundle if needed.

rules.title: Login without session_regenerate_id (session fixation)
rules.description: A login state is stored in the session, but the session id is never regenerated in this file.
rules.impact: An attacker who knows a visitor's session id before login can take over the account.
rules.remediation: Call session_regenerate_id(true) right after a successful login.

rules.title: Cookie set without security flags
rules.description: setcookie() is called with only a name and value, so HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite are missing.
rules.impact: Cookies can be read by scripts or sent over plain HTTP.
rules.remediation: Pass an options array: httponly => true, secure => true, samesite => "Lax".

rules.title: Form without CSRF protection
rules.description: A POST form exists and no CSRF token or similar protection was found in this file.
rules.impact: Another website can make a logged-in user submit actions without knowing.
rules.remediation: Add a per-session random token to every state-changing form and verify it on the server.

rules.title: Redirect target taken from user input
rules.description: The Location header uses request data without checking it.
rules.impact: Phishing: victims are sent from your trusted site to a malicious one.
rules.remediation: Only redirect to whitelisted paths or relative URLs.

rules.title: Permission decided by a user-controlled value
rules.description: A role, admin flag or login state is read directly from the request.
rules.impact: Anyone can give themselves admin rights by editing the URL or cookie.
rules.remediation: Decide permissions only from server-side session data checked against the database.

rules.title: Variables overwritten from user input
rules.description: extract(), $$variable or parse_str() without a second argument create variables from request data.
rules.impact: Attackers can overwrite internal variables, such as $isAdmin or file paths.
rules.remediation: Read only the specific keys you expect and validate them. Never use extract() on request data.

rules.title: Mail function called with user input (header injection)
rules.description: Request data is used in mail() arguments.
rules.impact: Attackers can add extra recipients or headers and send spam through your server.
rules.remediation: Validate the email with filter_var, strip line breaks, and use a mail library.

rules.title: XML external entity processing enabled
rules.description: The XML parser is configured to load external entities.
rules.impact: Attackers can read server files or make internal requests through crafted XML.
rules.remediation: Remove LIBXML_NOENT/LIBXML_DTDLOAD and never enable entity loading for untrusted XML.

rules.title: phpinfo() exposed
rules.description: phpinfo() prints the full server configuration, paths and modules.
rules.impact: Gives attackers detailed information to plan attacks.
rules.remediation: Remove phpinfo() calls from deployed code.

rules.title: Detailed errors or debug mode enabled
rules.description: Error messages and stack traces are shown to visitors.
rules.impact: Leaks file paths, SQL queries and secrets.
rules.remediation: Disable display_errors and APP_DEBUG in production; log errors to a file instead.

rules.title: allow_url_include enabled
rules.description: PHP is allowed to include code from remote URLs.
rules.impact: Turns any file inclusion bug into remote code execution.
rules.remediation: Set allow_url_include = Off.

rules.title: CORS allows every origin
rules.description: Any website may read responses from this application in a visitor's browser.
rules.impact: Data theft from logged-in users when combined with credentials or sensitive data.
rules.remediation: Allow only specific trusted origins.

rules.title: Insecure server configuration
rules.description: PHP version disclosure or directory listing is enabled.
rules.impact: Helps attackers find files and fingerprint the server.
rules.remediation: Set expose_php = Off and use "Options -Indexes".

rules.title: Secret key or private key committed in code
rules.description: A real-looking API key, access token or private key is stored in the source code.
rules.impact: Anyone with the code can use your cloud account, payment account or servers.
rules.remediation: Revoke the key now, create a new one, and load it from environment variables or a secret manager. Remove it from version history.

rules.title: Hard-coded password or secret
rules.description: A password or secret value is written directly in the source code.
rules.impact: Anyone who can read the code or repository gets access to the system.
rules.remediation: Move secrets to environment variables or a .env file outside version control and rotate the exposed value.

rules.title: Secret value in environment or config file
rules.description: A real-looking secret is stored in an environment file that is part of the project.
rules.impact: If this file is uploaded, shared or deployed in the web root, the secrets leak.
rules.remediation: Never ship .env files with real values. Keep them out of the project archive and the web root.

rules.title: Database password written in the connection call
rules.description: The database password is passed as a literal string.
rules.impact: Leaked source code gives direct database access.
rules.remediation: Read the credentials from environment variables or a protected config file.

rules.title: DOM XSS: untrusted data written into HTML
rules.description: Browser-side code puts URL or form data straight into the page as HTML.
rules.impact: Script injection in the visitor's browser.
rules.remediation: Use textContent, or sanitise with a library such as DOMPurify before inserting HTML.

rules.title: eval() or new Function() in JavaScript
rules.description: JavaScript builds and runs code from text at runtime.
rules.impact: Script injection if any part of the text can be influenced by a user.
rules.remediation: Replace with JSON.parse or normal functions.

rules.title: Authentication data stored in localStorage
rules.description: Tokens kept in web storage can be stolen by any script that runs on the page (XSS).
rules.impact: Account takeover after any XSS flaw.
rules.remediation: Prefer HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies for session tokens.

rules.title: target="_blank" without rel="noopener"
rules.description: Pages opened in a new tab can access the opener window.
rules.impact: Reverse tabnabbing / phishing.
rules.remediation: Add rel="noopener noreferrer".

rules.title: Raw SQL expression contains user request data
rules.description: A raw database query expression directly interpolates request data without parameter bindings.
rules.impact: SQL injection allowing data extraction, tampering or privilege escalation.
rules.remediation: Pass query parameters as a second array of bindings to DB::raw or whereRaw.

rules.title: Unrestricted Eloquent mass assignment ($guarded = [])
rules.description: Setting $guarded = [] disables mass assignment protection on the Eloquent model entirely.
rules.impact: Attackers can overwrite sensitive columns such as is_admin, role, or account balances via crafted HTTP payloads.
rules.remediation: Use explicit $fillable attributes on models instead of an empty $guarded array.

rules.title: Storage call uses unvalidated path from request
rules.description: Storage method is invoked with request data, which may allow path traversal ../ to read or delete arbitrary files.
rules.impact: Arbitrary file read or deletion across the server filesystem.
rules.remediation: Sanitize the filename with basename() and validate against an allow-list of directories.

rules.title: Unescaped Blade statement renders user request data
rules.description: Blade raw echo syntax {!! !!} bypasses HTML escaping and prints request data directly.
rules.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) allowing execution of arbitrary JavaScript in victim browsers.
rules.remediation: Use standard escaped Blade syntax {{ $var }} instead of unescaped {!! !!}.
